items.title: Setup
items.description: The token CSS, the appearance provider and the cn helper. Every other item needs it.

import { type ClassValue, clsx } from 'clsx';
import {
  type ClassValidator,
  type DefaultClassGroupIds,
  type DefaultThemeGroupIds,
  extendTailwindMerge,
  validators,
} from 'tailwind-merge';

/**
 * Custom `@theme` scale values nxds adds to built-in tailwind-merge
 * namespaces. Hand-mirrors the keys emitted by `@nxds/core` (see
 * `packages/tailwind`) and by co-located component CSS.
 */
export const NXDS_THEME_SCALES = {
  radius: ['base'],
  ease: ['enter', 'exit', 'move'],
  shadow: ['base', 'inner'],
  animate: ['progress-indeterminate'],
} satisfies Partial<Record<DefaultThemeGroupIds, string[]>>;

/**
 * nxds class names tailwind-merge does not know, keyed by the class group
 * each one extends, so a conflicting pair collapses to last-wins in `cn()`.
 */
export const NXDS_CLASS_GROUPS = {
  animate: ['animate-overlay-presence-exit'],
  duration: [
    'duration-0',
    'duration-faster',
    'duration-fast',
    'duration-default',
    'duration-moderate',
    'duration-slow',
    'duration-slower',
  ],
  // The two ring-safe colour transitions. Without this they land nowhere and a
  // later `transition-none` / `transition-all` fails to replace them.
  transition: ['transition-control', 'transition-field'],
  // Take any colour token, like `bg-*` / `text-*`.
  'autofill-bg': [{ 'autofill-bg': [validators.isAny] }],
  'autofill-text': [{ 'autofill-text': [validators.isAny] }],
  surface: [{ surface: [validators.isAny] }],
  'ring-color': ['ring-surface'],
  'ring-offset-color': ['ring-offset-surface'],
  z: ['z-overlay', 'z-sticky', 'z-modal', 'z-popover', 'z-toast', 'z-max'],
  gap: ['gap-container', 'gap-layout-section', 'gap-layout-stack'],
  p: ['p-container'],
  'border-w': [
    'border-thin',
    'border-default',
    'border-thick',
    'border-width-thin',
    'border-width-default',
    'border-width-thick',
  ],
  'border-w-x': [
    'border-x-thin',
    'border-x-default',
    'border-x-thick',
    'border-width-x-thin',
    'border-width-x-default',
    'border-width-x-thick',
  ],
  'border-w-y': [
    'border-y-thin',
    'border-y-default',
    'border-y-thick',
    'border-width-y-thin',
    'border-width-y-default',
    'border-width-y-thick',
  ],
  'border-w-t': [
    'border-t-thin',
    'border-t-default',
    'border-t-thick',
    'border-width-t-thin',
    'border-width-t-default',
    'border-width-t-thick',
  ],
  'border-w-r': [
    'border-r-thin',
    'border-r-default',
    'border-r-thick',
    'border-width-r-thin',
    'border-width-r-default',
    'border-width-r-thick',
  ],
  'border-w-b': [
    'border-b-thin',
    'border-b-default',
    'border-b-thick',
    'border-width-b-thin',
    'border-width-b-default',
    'border-width-b-thick',
  ],
  'border-w-l': [
    'border-l-thin',
    'border-l-default',
    'border-l-thick',
    'border-width-l-thin',
    'border-width-l-default',
    'border-width-l-thick',
  ],
  'border-w-s': [
    'border-s-thin',
    'border-s-default',
    'border-s-thick',
    'border-width-s-thin',
    'border-width-s-default',
    'border-width-s-thick',
  ],
  'border-w-e': [
    'border-e-thin',
    'border-e-default',
    'border-e-thick',
    'border-width-e-thin',
    'border-width-e-default',
    'border-width-e-thick',
  ],
  'border-w-bs': [
    'border-bs-thin',
    'border-bs-default',
    'border-bs-thick',
    'border-width-bs-thin',
    'border-width-bs-default',
    'border-width-bs-thick',
  ],
  'border-w-be': [
    'border-be-thin',
    'border-be-default',
    'border-be-thick',
    'border-width-be-thin',
    'border-width-be-default',
    'border-width-be-thick',
  ],
  'divide-x': ['divide-x-thin', 'divide-x-default', 'divide-x-thick'],
  'divide-y': ['divide-y-thin', 'divide-y-default', 'divide-y-thick'],
  // `outline-{thin,default,thick}` are widths, not colours. Without this they
  // land in tailwind-merge's `outline-color` group and a field's
  // `outline-focus-default` silently drops the width beside it.
  'outline-w': ['outline-thin', 'outline-default', 'outline-thick'],
  // Only the `@utility` aliases, which the emitted-utility drift guard in
  // `utils.test.ts` requires to declare a group. `border-border-*` is
  // Tailwind-generated from `--color-*` rather than emitted as a utility, and
  // tailwind-merge's default `theme.color` is `[isAny]`, so it needs no entry.
  'border-color': [
    'border-color-default',
    'border-color-default-alpha',
    'border-color-focus',
    'border-color-disabled',
    'border-color-warning',
    'border-color-warning-active',
    'border-color-success',
    'border-color-success-active',
    'border-color-error',
    'border-color-error-active',
    'border-color-information',
    'border-color-information-active',
    'border-color-primary',
    'border-color-primary-active',
  ],
  typography: [
    'typography-heading-large',
    'typography-heading-medium',
    'typography-heading-small',
    'typography-heading-xsmall',
    'typography-heading-xxsmall',
    'typography-body-default',
    'typography-body-small',
    'typography-shortcut',
    'typography-label-default',
    'typography-label-small',
    'typography-label-caps',
    'typography-code-block',
    'typography-code-inline',
  ],
} satisfies Partial<
  Record<
    | DefaultClassGroupIds
    | 'typography'
    | 'autofill-bg'
    | 'autofill-text'
    | 'surface',
    (string | Record<string, ClassValidator[]>)[]
  >
>;

type NxdsClassGroupId = keyof typeof NXDS_CLASS_GROUPS;

/**
 * The atomic class groups a `typography-*` composite overwrites. Every CSS
 * property the generated composites declare must map to a group listed here.
 */
export const TYPOGRAPHY_CONFLICTS = [
  'font-family',
  'font-size',
  'font-weight',
  'leading',
  'tracking',
  'text-wrap',
] satisfies DefaultClassGroupIds[];

/** Tailwind-merge configured with `nx:` prefix and nxds custom utility groups. */
const twMerge = extendTailwindMerge<NxdsClassGroupId>({
  prefix: 'nx',
  extend: {
    theme: NXDS_THEME_SCALES,
    classGroups: NXDS_CLASS_GROUPS,
    conflictingClassGroups: {
      typography: TYPOGRAPHY_CONFLICTS,
    },
  },
});

/**
 * Combines class names using clsx and tailwind-merge
 * Supports nx: prefixed Tailwind classes
 */
export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) {
  return twMerge(clsx(inputs));
}

items.name: accordion
items.title: Accordion
items.description: Accordion shows and hides stacked sections of content. Use it when readers need only some sections of a long page. For a single section, use Collapsible.

items.name: alert
items.title: Alert
items.description:
Alert shows a status message inside the page. Use it for information, success, warning and error messages. Compose the icon, text, actions and close button as children.

- Stack layout: use no actions, or one or two Button actions. Leave out AlertClose.
- Inline layout: use AlertClose alone, one or two Button actions, or Buttons plus AlertClose.
- AlertClose doesn't remove the alert. Remove it in your own `onClick` handler.

items.name: alert-dialog
items.title: AlertDialog
items.description: AlertDialog makes the user confirm or cancel before an action with serious results, such as deleting data. For lower-stakes modal tasks, use Dialog. For edge panels, use Sheet, or Drawer for drag-to-dismiss.

items.name: appearance
items.title: Appearance
items.description: NxdsAppearanceSettings is a full settings panel for theme, typography, layout feel and interaction preferences. Render it inside NxdsAppearanceProvider. For a compact popover, use NxdsThemeQuickControl.

items.name: aspect-ratio
items.title: AspectRatio
items.description: AspectRatio keeps its content at a fixed width-to-height ratio. Use it for images, video, embeds and maps. AspectRatio fills its parent width, so place it in a sized container.

items.name: attachment
items.title: Attachment
items.description: Attachment shows one file with its preview, name, size and upload state. Use it in upload queues and message composers. For a general list row, use Item.

items.name: avatar
items.title: Avatar
items.description: Avatar shows a person's profile image, with initials as the fallback. Use AvatarGroup to stack several people and AvatarStatus to show presence.

items.name: badge
items.title: Badge
items.description: Badge labels an item with a short status, category or count. It is not interactive. Pair a status color with text or an icon, because color alone doesn't carry meaning.

items.name: breadcrumb
items.title: Breadcrumb
items.description: Breadcrumb shows where the current page sits in your app's hierarchy. Use it on pages two or more levels deep. For top-level navigation, use NavigationMenu or Sidebar.

items.name: bubble
items.title: Bubble
items.description: Bubble shows one message in a conversation. Use it as the body of a chat or assistant turn. For the avatar, header and footer around it, use Message.

items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.description:
Button triggers an action. Use it for short, visible labels.

- Use one decorative icon slot at most: `startIcon` or `endIcon`.
- A loading button shows only a spinner and hides its icons.
- Icon-only buttons need `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

items.name: button-group
items.title: ButtonGroup
items.description: ButtonGroup joins related buttons into one cluster with shared borders. Use it for a set of related actions or a split button. For an input with addons, use InputGroup.

items.name: card
items.title: Card
items.description: Card groups related content and actions in a bordered section. Use it for dashboards, settings sections and forms. For a plain list row, use Item.

items.name: carousel
items.title: Carousel
items.description: Carousel shows a set of slides that readers move through one at a time. Use it for galleries and featured content. Install the `embla-carousel-react` peer dependency first.

items.name: chart
items.title: Chart
items.description: ChartContainer wraps a Recharts chart with nxds colors, tooltips and legends. Use it for bar, area and line charts. Set the label and color of each series in `config`.

items.name: checkbox
items.title: Checkbox
items.description: Checkbox selects one or more options, or toggles one setting. Its indeterminate state marks a partly selected group. Pair it with Label, or use ChoiceRow or ChoiceCard for richer option rows.

files.content:
import * as React from 'react';

import * as CheckboxPrimitive from '@radix-ui/react-checkbox';

import { IconCheck, IconMinus } from '../../lib/icons';
import { selectionIndicatorMotionClassName } from '../../lib/motion';
import { cn } from '../../lib/utils';

/**
 * CheckboxProps
 *
 * Props for the Checkbox component.
 */
type CheckboxProps = React.ComponentProps<typeof CheckboxPrimitive.Root>;

/**
 * Selects one or more options, or toggles one setting.
 * Set `checked="indeterminate"` to show a minus for a partly selected group, such as "select all".
 *
 * The box is 16px, so pair it with a label that carries the touch target.
 * Use `Label`, `ChoiceRow`, `ChoiceCard`, or `FieldLabel` in a `Field`.
 */
function Checkbox({ className, ...props }: CheckboxProps) {
  return (
    <CheckboxPrimitive.Root
      data-slot="checkbox"
      className={cn(
        'nx:group nx:peer nx:inline-flex nx:size-4 nx:shrink-0 nx:items-center nx:justify-center nx:p-0',
        'nx:rounded-sm nx:border-default nx:border-border-default nx:bg-container',
        'nx:transition-control',
        'nx:focus-visible:outline-2 nx:focus-visible:outline-focus-default',
        'nx:aria-invalid:border-error-border nx:aria-invalid:focus-visible:outline-focus-error',
        'nx:disabled:cursor-not-allowed nx:disabled:border-border-disabled nx:disabled:bg-disabled',
        'nx:enabled:data-[state=unchecked]:hover:bg-container-hover nx:enabled:data-[state=unchecked]:active:bg-container-active',
        'nx:data-[state=checked]:border-primary-background nx:data-[state=checked]:bg-primary-background nx:data-[state=checked]:text-primary-foreground',
        'nx:enabled:data-[state=checked]:hover:border-primary-background-hover nx:enabled:data-[state=checked]:hover:bg-primary-background-hover',
        'nx:enabled:data-[state=checked]:active:border-primary-background-hover nx:enabled:data-[state=checked]:active:bg-primary-background-active',
        'nx:data-[state=indeterminate]:border-primary-background nx:data-[state=indeterminate]:bg-primary-background nx:data-[state=indeterminate]:text-primary-foreground',
        'nx:enabled:data-[state=indeterminate]:hover:border-primary-background-hover nx:enabled:data-[state=indeterminate]:hover:bg-primary-background-hover',
        'nx:enabled:data-[state=indeterminate]:active:border-primary-background-hover nx:enabled:data-[state=indeterminate]:active:bg-primary-background-active',
        'nx:data-[state=checked]:disabled:border-primary-disabled nx:data-[state=checked]:disabled:bg-primary-disabled',
        'nx:data-[state=indeterminate]:disabled:border-primary-disabled nx:data-[state=indeterminate]:disabled:bg-primary-disabled',
        // Invalid + checked/indeterminate: aria-invalid is the single authoring hook.
        'nx:aria-invalid:data-[state=checked]:border-error-border nx:aria-invalid:data-[state=checked]:bg-error-background nx:aria-invalid:data-[state=checked]:text-error-foreground',
        'nx:aria-invalid:data-[state=indeterminate]:border-error-border nx:aria-invalid:data-[state=indeterminate]:bg-error-background nx:aria-invalid:data-[state=indeterminate]:text-error-foreground',
        'nx:enabled:aria-invalid:data-[state=checked]:hover:border-error-border nx:enabled:aria-invalid:data-[state=checked]:hover:bg-error-background-hover',
        'nx:enabled:aria-invalid:data-[state=checked]:active:border-error-border nx:enabled:aria-invalid:data-[state=checked]:active:bg-error-background-active',
        'nx:enabled:aria-invalid:data-[state=indeterminate]:hover:border-error-border nx:enabled:aria-invalid:data-[state=indeterminate]:hover:bg-error-background-hover',
        'nx:enabled:aria-invalid:data-[state=indeterminate]:active:border-error-border nx:enabled:aria-invalid:data-[state=indeterminate]:active:bg-error-background-active',
        className
      )}
      {...props}
    >
      <CheckboxPrimitive.Indicator
        forceMount
        data-slot="checkbox-indicator"
        className="nx:relative nx:flex nx:size-full nx:items-center nx:justify-center nx:text-current"
      >
        <IconCheck
          data-slot="checkbox-check"
          aria-hidden="true"
          className={cn(
            'nx:absolute nx:size-3.5',
            selectionIndicatorMotionClassName,
            'nx:group-data-[state=checked]:scale-100 nx:group-data-[state=checked]:opacity-100'
          )}
        />
        <IconMinus
          data-slot="checkbox-minus"
          aria-hidden="true"
          className={cn(
            'nx:absolute nx:size-3.5',
            selectionIndicatorMotionClassName,
            'nx:group-data-[state=indeterminate]:scale-100 nx:group-data-[state=indeterminate]:opacity-100'
          )}
        />
      </CheckboxPrimitive.Indicator>
    </CheckboxPrimitive.Root>
  );
}

export { Checkbox, type CheckboxProps };

export const selectionIndicatorMotionClassName =
  'nx:scale-50 nx:opacity-0 nx:transition-[opacity,scale] nx:duration-fast nx:ease-enter';

items.name: choice-card
items.title: ChoiceCard
items.description: ChoiceCard is a clickable card for a checkbox or radio choice with a title and description. The nested Checkbox or RadioGroupItem stays the only control. For a simple inline label use Label, and for compact options use ChoiceRow.

items.name: choice-row
items.title: ChoiceRow
items.description: ChoiceRow makes a whole row the click target for a checkbox or radio choice. The nested Checkbox or RadioGroupItem stays the real control. For a simple inline label use Label, and for a roomier card use ChoiceCard.

items.name: collapsible
items.title: Collapsible
items.description: Collapsible shows and hides one content region. Use it for a single expandable section. For a stacked set of sections, use Accordion.

items.name: combobox
items.title: Combobox
items.description: Combobox lets the user search a list and pick one option. Use it for lists too long to scan. For a short list without search, use Select.

items.name: command
items.title: Command
items.description: Command is a searchable list of actions with keyboard navigation. Use it for command palettes and quick search. For picking a form value, use Combobox.

items.name: context-menu
items.title: ContextMenu
items.description: ContextMenu shows a menu of actions when the user right-clicks an area. Use it for actions on a specific item or region. For a menu opened by a button, use DropdownMenu.

files.content:
export const selectionIndicatorMotionClassName =
  'nx:scale-50 nx:opacity-0 nx:transition-[opacity,scale] nx:duration-fast nx:ease-enter';

items.name: date-picker
items.title: DatePicker
items.description: DatePicker shows a calendar grid for picking one date, a range or several dates. Install `react-day-picker` in your app to use it. If your Next.js app uses Cache Components, render DatePicker inside `<Suspense>` so it can read today's date.

items.name: description-list
items.title: DescriptionList
items.description:
DescriptionList shows metadata as term and value pairs.

- Wrap each term and its value in a DescriptionListItem.
- Format values and missing-value text yourself.
- Put actions inside DescriptionListDescription.
- Rows stack in narrow containers and form two columns when the list has room.

items.name: dialog
items.title: Dialog
items.description:
Dialog opens a modal for a task that interrupts the page. The user can dismiss it without making a choice.

- If the user must confirm or cancel a consequential action, use AlertDialog.
- For a panel at the screen edge, such as settings or filters, use Sheet.
- For a mobile-style panel with drag-to-dismiss, use Drawer.

items.name: drawer
items.title: Drawer
items.description:
Drawer slides in a panel from a screen edge that the user can drag to dismiss. Use it for mobile-style panels, especially bottom drawers. Install `vaul` in your app to use it.

- For a side panel without drag gestures, use Sheet.
- For a centered modal task, use Dialog.
- For a confirmation that forces a choice, use AlertDialog.
- Set `showHandle={false}` on DrawerContent to remove the handle and its spacing. Dragging and dismissal stay the same.

items.name: dropdown-menu
items.title: DropdownMenu
items.description: DropdownMenu opens a list of actions from a button. Use it for a short list of actions or options. For picking a form value, use Select.

files.content:
export const selectionIndicatorMotionClassName =
  'nx:scale-50 nx:opacity-0 nx:transition-[opacity,scale] nx:duration-fast nx:ease-enter';

items.name: empty-state
items.title: EmptyState
items.description: EmptyState explains why a list, table or record view has no content yet. Give it an icon, a title, a short description and an optional action.

items.name: field
items.title: Field
items.description: Field lays out a label, control, description and error as one form field. Use it for any labeled form control. For a group of related fields, wrap them in FieldSet or FieldGroup.

items.name: filter-builder
items.title: FilterBuilder
items.description:
FilterBuilder edits filter conditions inside nested All and Any groups. Pass the tree as `value` and update it in `onValueChange`. For a row of applied filters, use FilterCondition or FilterChip.

- Drafts can be incomplete. Call `getFilterErrors` to validate text, number, date and choice fields.
- An empty root means no filters. An empty nested group is invalid.
- The root is depth zero, and `maxDepth` defaults to 3.
- Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD` strings. Numbers stay as draft strings.
- Every ID must be unique. Field and option IDs must not be empty.
- Set `operators` on a field to limit its operators.
- Your app owns Apply and Cancel, running the query, URLs, permissions and fetching.
- See the Filtering pattern for grouped conditions and where the app takes over.

items.name: filter-chip
items.title: FilterChip
items.description:
FilterChip is a button that removes an applied filter. Use it in a row of applied filters chosen in a menu or panel. For passive metadata use Badge, and for a condition the user edits use FilterCondition.

- Clicking the label or × removes the filter. It never opens an editor or toggles a choice.
- Give it a full `aria-label`, such as "Remove status filter: Paid".
- Your app owns the filter values. After removal, move focus to the next chip, the previous chip or a stable filter control.
- Long labels truncate on screen but keep their full accessible name.
- It has one compact size that follows the density setting.

items.name: filter-condition
items.title: FilterCondition
items.description:
FilterCondition shows one filter as separate field, operator, value and remove parts. Use it when the user edits a filter from its summary. For a chip that only removes, use FilterChip.

- Wrap each FilterConditionSegment in a PopoverTrigger or DropdownMenuTrigger with `asChild`.
- Your app owns open state, draft values, when changes apply and focus after removal.
- All parts share one compact height that follows density. There is no `size` prop.
- Editor inputs set their own size.
- Segments are native buttons, so Enter and Space activate them.
- The full summary stays accessible when it truncates on screen.
- See Patterns/Filtering for recipes that apply changes at once or on Apply.

items.name: hide
items.title: Hide
items.description: Hide removes its children from view above or below a viewport or container width. Use it for responsive visibility instead of toggling `nx:hidden` classes. To show content only at a width, use Show.

items.name: hover-card
items.title: HoverCard
items.description: HoverCard shows a preview card when the user hovers or focuses a trigger. Use it for profile and link previews. For content opened by a click, use Popover.

items.name: input
items.title: Input
items.description: Input collects one line of text. Give every input a visible label or an `aria-label`. For several lines of text, use Textarea.

items.name: input-group
items.title: InputGroup
items.description: InputGroup frames an input or textarea with icons, text, buttons or key hints in one field. Use it for search boxes, URL prefixes and inline actions. For a plain field, use Input.

items.name: input-otp
items.title: InputOTP
items.description: InputOTP collects a one-time code, with one slot per character. Use it for verification and sign-in codes. For other short text, use Input.

items.name: item
items.title: Item
items.description: Item lays out a row with media, a title, a description and actions. Use it for file lists, settings rows and search results. For tabular data, use Table.

items.name: kbd
items.title: Kbd
items.description: Kbd shows a keyboard key, such as `Esc` or `⌘`. Use it to document shortcuts. For a key combination, wrap several Kbd elements in KbdGroup.

items.name: label
items.title: Label
items.description: Label names a form control. Set `htmlFor` to the control's `id` so a click on the label focuses or toggles the control. Inside a Field, use FieldLabel.

items.name: marker
items.title: Marker
items.description: Marker labels a point in a list, feed or message stream with muted text and an optional icon. Use it for dates, edit notes and progress updates. For a rule with no label, use Separator.

items.name: menubar
items.title: Menubar
items.description: Menubar shows a row of menus that stays on screen, like a desktop app. Use it for app-level commands grouped under File, Edit and View. For one menu on a button, use DropdownMenu.

files.content:
export const selectionIndicatorMotionClassName =
  'nx:scale-50 nx:opacity-0 nx:transition-[opacity,scale] nx:duration-fast nx:ease-enter';

items.name: message
items.title: Message
items.description: Message lays out one conversation turn, with an avatar, a header, a body and a footer. Use it for chat and assistant threads, with Bubble or Attachment as the body. Message holds no chat state, so your app owns the messages and MessageScroller handles scrolling.

items.name: message-scroller
items.title: MessageScroller
items.description: MessageScroller scrolls a message stream and keeps the latest turn in view. Use it for chat and assistant threads that grow as new turns arrive. For other scrolling content, use ScrollArea.

items.name: multi-select
items.title: MultiSelect
items.description: MultiSelect lets the user search a list and pick several options, shown as chips. Use it for tags, filters and other choices with several answers. For one option, use Combobox or Select.

items.name: native-select
items.title: NativeSelect
items.description: NativeSelect styles the browser `<select>`, so mobile users get the system picker. Use it for dense forms and long, plain lists. For a styled dropdown use Select, and for search use Combobox.

items.name: navigation-menu
items.title: NavigationMenu
items.description: NavigationMenu shows top-level site links, with flyout panels for groups of pages. Use it for a website header. For app commands, use Menubar.

items.name: page-header
items.title: PageHeader
items.description:
PageHeader titles a page or section, with optional metadata, status, description and actions. Compact, standard and detail headers are compositions of the same parts, not variants.

- The title renders an `h1`. Use `asChild` to pick another heading level.
- For a larger title, add `className="nx:typography-heading-large"` to PageHeaderTitle.
- Put page headers inside `main` and section headers inside their `section`.
- Actions wrap below the content in narrow containers. Your app owns what they do.

items.name: pagination
items.title: Pagination
items.description: Pagination links to the pages of a long list or table. Use it when results are split across pages. Your app decides which page numbers to show.

items.name: popover
items.title: Popover
items.description: Popover opens a floating panel next to a trigger. Use it for short forms and extra controls. For a hover hint, use Tooltip, and for a list of actions, use DropdownMenu.

items.name: progress
items.title: Progress
items.description: Progress shows how far along a task is, such as an upload or a multi-step form. Leave out `value` for an animated bar while the total is unknown. Always give it an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

items.name: radio-group
items.title: RadioGroup
items.description:
RadioGroup lets the user pick one option from a short, visible list. For a long list, use Select.

- For a plain text label, pair each RadioGroupItem with Label.
- For a compact clickable row, wrap each item in ChoiceRow.
- For a card with a title and description, wrap each item in ChoiceCard.

items.name: resizable
items.title: Resizable
items.description: Resizable splits an area into panels that users resize by dragging or with the keyboard. Use it for layouts like a sidebar beside an editor. Give every `ResizableHandle` an `aria-label`.

items.name: scroll-area
items.title: ScrollArea
items.description: ScrollArea gives a fixed-size region custom scrollbars that look the same on every platform. Use it for panels, lists and drawers with overflowing content. For a full page, let the browser scroll the page.

items.name: select
items.title: Select
items.description: Select lets users pick one option from a styled dropdown. Use it when the list needs a styled trigger and menu that match the rest of the UI. For native form submission and OS pickers with plain text options, use NativeSelect.

items.name: separator
items.title: Separator
items.description: Separator draws a thin rule between groups of content. Use `orientation="vertical"` inside a flex row with a set height. Set `decorative={false}` when the rule marks a real boundary that screen readers should announce.

items.name: sheet
items.title: Sheet
items.description: Sheet slides a panel in from one edge of the viewport. Use it for settings, filters, navigation or supporting forms. For a centered task use Dialog, for a forced choice use AlertDialog, and for drag-to-dismiss use Drawer.

items.name: show
items.title: Show
items.description: Show displays its children only above or below a viewport or container width. Use it for responsive visibility instead of toggling `nx:hidden` classes. To hide content at a width, use Hide.

items.name: sidebar
items.title: Sidebar
items.description: Sidebar is the app's main navigation panel. It collapses to an icon rail or off screen, and opens as a Sheet on narrow screens. Wrap the app shell in `SidebarProvider` and put the page content in `SidebarInset`.

items.name: skeleton
items.title: Skeleton
items.description: Skeleton shows a pulsing placeholder where content is still loading. Use it to keep the layout steady until data arrives. For a short wait with no known layout, use Spinner.

items.name: slider
items.title: Slider
items.description: Slider sets a number, or a range with two thumbs, by dragging along a track or with the arrow keys. Use it for settings such as volume or brightness. Give each slider an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

items.name: sonner
items.title: Sonner
items.description: Toaster shows short, temporary notifications. Mount it once near your app root, then call `toast()` from anywhere. For a message that stays on the page, use Alert.

items.name: spinner
items.title: Spinner
items.description: Spinner shows that something is loading. Use it for page loads, "loading more" rows and Suspense fallbacks. For a loading Button, use its `loading` prop.

items.name: switch
items.title: Switch
items.description: Switch turns a setting on or off right away, with no save step. Pair it with a Label so the label text is clickable too. For a choice that waits for a Save button, use Checkbox.

items.name: table
items.title: Table
items.description: Table shows rows of data in columns. Use it for records users scan and compare, such as invoices. Sorting, selection and pagination logic stay in your app.

items.name: tabs
items.title: Tabs
items.description: Tabs switch between panels of related content in one place. Use them to split a view into sections that users visit one at a time.

items.name: textarea
items.title: Textarea
items.description: Textarea takes multi-line text, such as notes or a bio. It accepts every native textarea attribute. For a single line, use Input.

items.name: toggle
items.title: Toggle
items.description: Toggle is a button that stays pressed until clicked again, such as Bold. Icon-only toggles need an `aria-label`. For a set of related toggles, use ToggleGroup.

items.name: toggle-group
items.title: ToggleGroup
items.description: ToggleGroup is a set of related toggles, such as text alignment or Bold, Italic and Underline. Use `type="single"` for one choice or `type="multiple"` for several. Icon-only items need an `aria-label`.

items.name: toolbar
items.title: Toolbar
items.description:
Toolbar groups related controls behind one Tab stop. Arrow keys move between controls, and Home and End jump to the first and last. For actions that each need their own Tab stop, use a row of Buttons.

- Label the toolbar with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Build it from ToolbarButton, ToolbarLink, ToolbarToggleGroup and ToolbarToggleItem so every control joins the arrow-key order.
- ToolbarButton and ToolbarLink take Button `variant` and `size`, but not `loading` or icon slots.
- Use `asChild` to make a toolbar control a menu trigger.
- Keep text fields outside the toolbar, because arrow keys would conflict with typing.
- In narrow containers, controls wrap in DOM order and arrow keys still reach every row.
- Your app owns the commands, selection, visibility and placement.

items.name: tooltip
items.title: Tooltip
items.description: Tooltip shows a short hint when users hover over or focus a trigger. Use it for brief labels, such as the name of an icon button. Wrap a group of tooltips in `TooltipProvider` to share one open delay.

items.name: inline-edit
items.title: InlineEdit
items.description: InlineEdit edits one line of text in place, saving with Enter or Save. Use it for a single field on a detail view, such as a name. For several fields use a form with Field, and for longer text use Textarea.

items.name: choice-filter
items.title: ChoiceFilter
items.description: ChoiceFilter filters by one value from a short list and applies it at once. Use it for a few mutually exclusive options. To match several values, use MultiChoiceFilter.

items.name: date-range-filter
items.title: DateRangeFilter
items.description: DateRangeFilter filters by a range of calendar days, applied when users press Apply. Use it for created, updated or due dates. Presets cover common ranges, and the calendar covers the rest. If your Next.js app uses Cache Components, render DateRangeFilter inside `<Suspense>` so it can read today's date.

items.name: multi-choice-filter
items.title: MultiChoiceFilter
items.description: MultiChoiceFilter filters by several values from a list, applied when users press Apply. Use it when a record can match any of several values. For one quick choice, use ChoiceFilter.

items.name: number-comparison-filter
items.title: NumberComparisonFilter
items.description: NumberComparisonFilter compares one number with equals, not equals, greater than or less than. Use it for a single threshold, such as an amount. For a range with both ends, use NumberRangeFilter.

items.name: number-range-filter
items.title: NumberRangeFilter
items.description: NumberRangeFilter filters by a number between a minimum and a maximum. Use it when both ends matter, such as a price band. For a single threshold, use NumberComparisonFilter.

items.name: text-filter
items.title: TextFilter
items.description: TextFilter filters records whose text contains, equals, does not equal or starts with a value, or is empty or not empty. Use it for free-text fields such as names or titles. For a fixed set of values, use ChoiceFilter or MultiChoiceFilter.
